question: What bone forms the posterior boundary of the pelvic floor attachment?
explanation: The pelvic floor attaches posteriorly to the coccyx and anteriorly to the pubic bone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why is the pelvic floor shaped like a funnel?

options.A: It slopes downward and inward to support pelvic organs
options.B: It narrows sharply at the level of the true pelvis
options.C: It connects the abdominal cavity directly to the perineal skin
options.D: It expands outward to accommodate fluid accumulation

explanation: The funnel shape allows the muscular hammock to cradle internal organs effectively while allowing passage for tubular structures. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which muscle group forms the main supportive sling of the pelvic floor?
explanation: The levator ani muscle group provides the primary muscular support and continence mechanism for the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h2)

question: A patient loses the supportive function of the puborectalis muscle. What problem occurs?
explanation: The puborectalis forms a sling around the anorectal junction, playing a major role in maintaining fecal continence. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which ligament mainly prevents uterine prolapse by anchoring the cervix laterally?
explanation: The cardinal ligaments extend from the lateral cervix and vagina to the lateral pelvic walls, providing primary structural suspension. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the main job of pelvic fascial layers alongside the muscles?

options.A: Regulating local blood pressure via vasoconstriction
options.B: Providing passive suspension and anchoring for organs
options.C: Producing synovial fluid for joint lubrication

explanation: Fascia and ligaments act as passive support networks that keep pelvic organs in their correct anatomical positions. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is an important job of the pelvic floor when you cough or sneeze?

options.D: Releasing hormones to regulate fluid balance

explanation: The pelvic floor contracts reflexively to support organs against sudden increases in abdominal pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h4)

question: How does the pelvic floor assist the fetus during vaginal delivery?

options.A: It guides the fetal head downward and outward through the birth canal
options.B: It secretes lubricating mucus to speed up labor
options.C: It pushes the placenta out before the baby descends
options.D: It completely relaxes to let the baby drop without resistance

explanation: The sloping muscular hammock helps rotate and direct the presenting part of the fetus during childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h4)

question: What condition occurs when pelvic structures bulge into the vaginal canal due to weakened support?
explanation: Prolapse happens when the supportive fascia and muscles give way, causing pelvic organs to descend from their normal positions. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h5)

question: A patient experiences pain during intercourse and difficulty emptying her bladder due to a constantly tight pelvic floor. What is this issue called?
explanation: Hypertonic pelvic floor muscles remain in a state of high tension, causing pain and obstructive urinary symptoms. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h5)

question: Which maneuver should a nurse ask a patient to perform to visualize potential pelvic organ prolapse?
explanation: Bearing down increases intra-abdominal pressure, helping make underlying prolapse visible during physical inspection. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why is taking a detailed pregnancy history important when evaluating pelvic floor health?

options.A: Past pregnancies predict the exact muscle fiber type in the levator ani
options.B: Prior pregnancies rule out the possibility of hypertonic pelvic pain
options.C: Vaginal deliveries and perineal trauma are major risk factors for floor weakness
options.D: Obstetric history determines whether the patient has pelvic infections

explanation: Stretching and tearing of nerves and muscles during childbirth frequently contribute to later pelvic floor dysfunction. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is another common name for pelvic floor muscle training exercises?
explanation: Kegel exercises involve repeated voluntary contraction and relaxation of the pelvic floor muscles to build strength. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why must nurses instruct patients to avoid squeezing their buttocks or thighs during pelvic floor training?

options.A: To prevent the development of painful muscle cramps in the legs
options.B: To ensure isolation and proper strengthening of the actual pelvic muscles
options.C: To keep the patient from holding their breath during the exercise
options.D: To reduce the overall energy expenditure of the routine

explanation: Using secondary muscle groups prevents effective targeting of the levator ani and delays rehabilitation progress. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h7)
